messages:
Ariane: Heads-up — after the middleweight rollout at 09:12 we see /v1/generate p99 jump ~600ms, p95 up ~120ms, p50 basically flat. Not sure if this is routing or batching related.
Jon: Saw the same on my end for EU region. p99 spike only for one endpoint shard, others look normal.
Meera: Can you paste the dashboard slice? which aggregation mode? raw-counts or tdigest? :eyes:
Ariane: Using console default rollup (tdigest). Quick snapshot: p50 120ms -> 125ms, p95 230ms -> 350ms, p99 380ms -> 980ms for endpoint=/v1/generate, route=chat, origin=canary
Sam: That looks like fallback noise. Did traffic shift between model variants or fallback weight change during rollout?
Ariane: We adjusted fallback weight from 0.05 -> 0.12 during traffic ramp at ~09:10.
Jon: If fallback variant has cold KV cache or different batching, that can blow up tail without moving median.
Meera: Agree. Two hypotheses: (1) fallback variant runs on different instance type with longer kernel latency; (2) sample attribution in dashboard is bundling fallback requests under the main route.
Ariane: Good point on attribution — we only have "route" tag, not variant. Console shows variant only in the rollouts panel currently.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout middleweight/v1 -> weight=12% applied by Meera at 09:09:44
Sam: We should surface sample counts by variant in the percentile panel. Right now p99 is noisy at low counts.
UIEmily: UX ask: add a tiny badge next to percentile lines that shows sample count and effective weight (e.g., 243 samples · 12%). Click to expand into per-variant breakdown.
Meera: Short-term investigative query (promql-ish):

```
sum by (variant) (rate(request_latency_bucket{endpoint="/v1/generate",le="+Inf"}[5m]))
/ sum by (variant) (rate(requests_total{endpoint="/v1/generate"}[5m]))
```

This gives sample rate split; also pull kv_cache_hit_rate by variant.
Jon: Also check batching distribution. Simple SQL to fetch token counts per request bucket:

```
SELECT bucket, count(*) FROM requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND variant IN ('main','fallback') GROUP BY bucket;
```

Ariane: I ran a quick slice: fallback variant p99 ~1.2s, kv_cache_hit_rate 18% vs main 82%, median tokens/request similar.
Sam: That explains it. Low kv cache and maybe no continuous batching warmup.
Meera: Longer-term: platform should annotate percentiles with provenance metadata: sample_count, variant_weights, kv_cache_hit_rate, batching_mode. We can auto-hide percentiles when sample_count < threshold and surface a warning.
UIEmily: UX proposal: show a subtle warning icon on p99 if sample_count < 500 in the time window, with tooltip: "p99 based on 312 samples across 2 variants — one variant has low cache hits and contributes the tail." Click opens variant split.
Jon: Ops ask: can we add a small endpoint-level health rule to flag sudden p99 divergence from p50 (>4x) and create a lightweight alert with sample provenance link?
Ariane: For immediate mitigation, Meera can we temporarily pin routing to main for this rollout until we fix fallback infra?
Meera: Yes — I'll reduce fallback weight to 3% and trigger a circuit-breaker if p99 stays >800ms for >3 min.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Routing weight change enacted: fallback weight set to 3% by Meera at 09:27:01
Ariane: After change p99 trending down (current ~420ms) — keep monitoring.
Sam: Action items:
- Meera: investigate fallback instance sizing and kv warmup (infra ticket).
- Jon: add a one-off query in runbook to split percentiles by variant and kv_cache_hit_rate.
- UIEmily + Platform: small UX badge + sample-count warning for p99 (spike visibility) — prioritize low-effort variant split first.
- Ariane: monitor for 15m then decide to continue rollout.
Meera: I'll open infra ticket INF-3421 and link to this thread.
Ariane: Thanks all :thumbsup:
